note: The main banks are Banco de la Nación Argentina, Banco Galicia and Banco Santander Argentina, the largest by deposits, with BBVA Argentina, already written, kept; each one's cards were read from the central bank's transparency register (its API for credit cards, read 30 October 2026), which every bank reports to. Banco de la Nación Argentina reports one personal card, its Visa Internacional, written as before: a maximum effective annual rate of 101.33% on financing, a maximum monthly administration fee of 10,446.99 pesos and a yearly renewal fee of 185,740.00, both at list price (its own schedule of charges gives them with VAT as 10,447.00 and 185,740.00). Banco Galicia (information of 15 October 2026) and Banco Santander Argentina (27 October 2026) each report twelve cards: for each, the maximum monthly administration and maintenance fee and the maximum yearly renewal fee at list price, and the maximum effective annual rates on financing and on cash advances, written as effective rates (105.81% at Galicia, 110.49% at Santander). BBVA Argentina reports eleven cards (9 October 2026), each with its maximum monthly administration fee and no renewal fee; its own table of card rates (in force October 2026) gives every card a nominal 66.67% a year on financing and on cash advances, written as the rate (the register's effective 89.68% is the same rate compounded); the Signature Travel, All and Save cards take the Visa Signature's rate, the table naming the Signature once; the Visa Nacional and MasterCard Regional it also lists aren't in the register and have no published fees, so they aren't written. The table's punitive interest (66.67%) is charged on top of the ordinary rate and isn't written as a penalty rate. The register states no minimum payment, grace period, late fee or foreign transaction fee; fees are at list price, before any discount, and VAT on them isn't written. No minimum payment is published for Banco de la Nación's, BBVA Argentina's, Banco Galicia's and Banco Santander Argentina's cards; tried (wave 5, 30 October 2026): every document this file cites, downloaded again on 30 October 2026 and searched for a minimum payment, states none for them; a search in Spanish for these banks' minimum payment found only BBVA Argentina's own explainer, which says the share depends on the bank and gives no figure; no rule of the Banco Central de la República Argentina setting a share was found (its transparency regime, cited here, carries none); archive.org's availability API, asked for each of the 4 documents this file cites, names a snapshot for 3 of them, which can't be read, web.archive.org being refused from here.
